red_tests.failure_fingerprint: checked == [] and empty hook output — for a new-branch push with no remote-tracking base, .githooks/pre-push computed OLDEST_UNPUSHED as the ROOT seed commit and built RANGE='<root>^..<head>'; '<root>^' does not resolve, the fatal rev-list error was swallowed by '|| true', NEW_COMMITS came back empty, and the gate exited 0 having validated NOTHING (assertion 'checked == [<head>]' fails on []).

force-push rewind (remote_sha valid, local_sha an ancestor of it) produced an empty remote..local range, so the hook exited 0 without validating anything — 'Checking TDD governance and provenance for KAN-250' missing from output.

rationale: KAN-257: the pre-push gate was a silent no-op for new-branch pushes with no remote-tracking base (CI/sandbox): the '<oldest-unpushed>^..<head>' fallback is fatal when the oldest unpublished commit is the repository ROOT seed commit, the swallowed error emptied NEW_COMMITS, and the gate validated nothing. The fix validates exactly the pushed tip when no base resolves (tip^..tip, bare SHA when the tip is itself a root), closes the force-push rewind free pass by validating the rewound tip, and reports the full SHA in the Checking line so the pinned observable (full 40-char SHA, per the KAN-218 test contract) is emitted. tests/test_pre_push_hook.py is deliberately NOT listed in test_files: it is byte-identical to main by the KAN-257 review contract (git diff main -- tests/test_pre_push_hook.py must be empty), and the staged provenance gate rejects manifest entries whose test file does not change in the baseline commit — its frozen state is enforced by that contract instead of a hash binding. The new tests/test_pre_push_hook_matrix.py pins the remaining behaviour-matrix cells (rewind validates, multi-ref accumulation, root-tip range resolution).
